plan.title: Treated vs control kidney DE with batch in design
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is which genes differ between 6 treated and 6 control human kidney samples quantified by Salmon, with two known processing batches balanced across conditions. Because each batch holds both conditions, batch is estimable separately from condition and enters the model as a fixed design term (batch + condition) rather than being corrected before testing. The plan follows the grounded procedure: sample-structure QC on blind variance-stabilized values first (PCA and sample distances colored by condition and batch confirm balance and flag outliers), a minimal low-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors inside the DESeq2 negative binomial model, the Wald test on the condition coefficient with apeglm LFC shrinkage for reporting, BH at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering, and an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as a second method because 6 replicates per group is at the low end of reliable power — the intersection of the two gene sets is the high-confidence answer (R-0042@54e1). The report carries both unshrunken and shrunken fold changes, MA and dispersion diagnostics, and the method-overlap summary. Only gene-level counts exist in this dataset (no transcript-level Salmon output), so tximport length offsets (R-0018) cannot be applied; this limitation is stated rather than worked around. The question does not ask for pathway or gene-set analysis, so no enrichment step is planned.
